memoryText: And these words that I command you today shall be on your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Deuteronomy 6:6-7 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
These two verses follow the Shema and describe how love for God is meant to be lived out. They are among the most practical verses in the Bible.

“These words that I command you today shall be on your heart.” The order matters. Before anything is taught to anyone else, the words must be on your own heart. A parent, teacher, or leader cannot pass on what he does not possess. The heart is the starting point.

“You shall teach them diligently to your children.” The word “diligently” means to sharpen, as one sharpens a blade. It suggests repetition and care. Faith is not passed on by accident. It requires intention and effort. Notice that the commandment is addressed to parents. God’s design is for faith to be taught at home first.

“And shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.” This is the surprising part. The teaching is not limited to a scheduled lesson. It is woven into the whole day: sitting, walking, going to bed, getting up. Every part of life becomes a moment to speak of God.

For the Christian, the verses call us to make Scripture and prayer part of our household. It is a ministry for parents, but also for grandparents, aunts, uncles, church members, and friends. In Christ, the whole community of believers shares the task of passing on the faith to the next generation.
weekInReview: This week you read the opening sermons of Deuteronomy. You saw how Moses looked back at the wilderness, how he restated the Ten Commandments, and how he gave the Shema, the greatest commandment. You read about God’s choice of Israel, not because of their righteousness, and about Moses’ intercession after the golden calf. You prayed through Psalm 78, which tells the whole story from the exodus to David as a lesson for the next generation. You read the first laws about worship, false prophets, clean foods, and the tithe. The week taught that obedience flows from love, that faith must be passed on at home, and that God’s grace is not based on our merit.
reflectionQuestions: The Shema says that God is one and calls for love with heart, soul, and might. Which of these three, heart, soul, or might, is the hardest for you to give, and why?
Moses told Israel three times that God’s gift was “not because of your righteousness.” How does Christ’s work on your behalf give you the same assurance?
Deuteronomy 6 says to teach faith “when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way.” What is one practical step you could take this week to talk about God in the course of ordinary life?
prayerPrompts: Ask God to put his words on your heart and help you teach them to those near you.
Thank him that his love is not based on your merit.
